title: DFT geometry optimization and ground‑state calculation
action: Using the TGS crystal structure from COD, perform a full DFT geometry optimization (atomic positions and, if needed, cell parameters) with the PBEsol functional and a plane‑wave cutoff of ~340 eV. Then run a self‑consistent field (SCF) calculation to obtain the ground‑state charge density and wavefunctions. Save the final relaxed structure.
description: Required intermediate: the optimized geometry and ground‑state charge density are needed by all subsequent property calculations.

title: Electronic band structure computation
action: Using the relaxed geometry and ground‑state density, perform a non‑self‑consistent band structure calculation along the high‑symmetry path Γ–Y–B–D–Γ. Write the band energies at each k‑point to band_structure.csv.
description: CSV file containing the band energies along the selected k‑path. The checker recomputes the indirect band gap from this file.
output_schema: CSV with columns: kpoint_label, kx, ky, kz, band_1, band_2, ..., band_n (one column per sorted energy band; energies in eV).

title: Total density of states computation
action: Using the relaxed geometry and ground‑state charge density, compute the total electronic density of states (DOS) on a uniform energy grid and write it to total_dos.csv.
description: CSV file with total DOS vs energy. The checker verifies the presence of a gap near the expected energy.

title: Projected density of states computation
action: Using the same ground‑state calculation, compute the projected density of states by orbital (s, p) and by element (O, C, N, H, S) and save the result to projected_dos.csv.
description: CSV with projected DOS. The checker verifies dominant p‑character (~80%) near the VBM and element‑resolved contributions.
output_schema: CSV with columns: energy (eV), s_dos, p_dos, O_dos, C_dos, N_dos, H_dos, S_dos (states/eV).

title: Dielectric function computation with scissor correction
action: Using the ground‑state wavefunctions, compute the frequency‑dependent dielectric tensor ε_ij(ω). Apply a scissor shift of 0.9 eV to the conduction bands. Write the real (ε1) and imaginary (ε2) diagonal components to dielectric_function.csv.
description: Scissor‑corrected dielectric function. The checker identifies the epsilon2_xx peak in the 5–10 eV range and compares to the hidden paper value.
output_schema: CSV with columns: energy (eV), epsilon1_xx, epsilon1_yy, epsilon1_zz, epsilon2_xx, epsilon2_yy, epsilon2_zz (all dimensionless).
